Synthetic benchmark sources

Source: R/dsg_benchmark.R
dsg_synthetic.Rd

Synthetic streams commonly used in stream learning, as defined in the river library, turned into dsg_source_regions() sources: their concept functions give the real drift states, and regional sub-sampling gives the virtual drift states (Hinder et al., 2026).

  • dsg_sea(): three features uniform in [0, 10]; label x1 + x2 > theta with theta in 8, 9, 7 and 9.5 (Street and Kim, 2001).

  • dsg_agrawal(): the nine features of the loan application generator of Agrawal et al. (1993) and its classification functions 0 to 8.

  • dsg_sine(): two features uniform in [0, 1] and the four SINE functions.

  • dsg_mixed(): two Boolean (x1, x2) and two numeric (x3, x4) features and the two MIXED functions.

Usage

dsg_sea(...)

dsg_agrawal(...)

dsg_sine(...)

dsg_mixed(...)

Arguments

...

Arguments for dsg_source_regions() and dsg_source(), such as n_clusters, n_variants or test_size.

Value

dsg_source object

References

Agrawal, R., Imielinski, T., and Swami, A. (1993). Database mining: a performance perspective. IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering, 5(6), 914-925.

Street, W. N., and Kim, Y. (2001). A streaming ensemble algorithm (SEA) for large-scale classification. In KDD 2001, 377-382.

Gama, J., Medas, P., Castillo, G., and Rodrigues, P. (2004). Learning with drift detection. In SBIA 2004, 286-295.

Montiel, J. et al. (2021). River: machine learning for streaming data in Python. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 22(110), 1-8.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dsg_take(dsg_agrawal(), 3)
#> $x
#>      salary commission age elevel car zipcode   hvalue hyears      loan

#> 2  31535.43   62586.92  55      0  10       2 804254.7     30 313643.36
#> 3  69847.39   82028.01  20      1   8       2 848886.4      5  57905.65
#> 
#> $y
#> [1] 1 0 1
